title: Data Labeling Workforce Welfare Pattern
description: A pattern for setting and independently auditing wage floors, content-exposure limits, and psychological-support access for any workforce labeling graphic or traumatic content, whether employed directly or through an outsourcing vendor.

history.note: Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources).

problem: AI safety and content-moderation classifiers require large volumes of human-labeled examples of harmful content, and this labor is often outsourced to lower-cost markets where wage, exposure, and psychological-support standards are set contractually but not independently verified in practice.
solution: Set a documented wage floor, a maximum daily/weekly exposure limit for graphic content review, and mandatory access to psychological support as contractual requirements for any data-labeling vendor, and conduct independent (not vendor-self-reported) audits of actual working conditions on a recurring basis.
applicability: Any organization that contracts, directly or via a vendor, a workforce to label graphic, traumatic, or otherwise psychologically harmful content for training or safety-classifier purposes.
consequences: Independent audits of outsourced labor add cost and require access the client may not contractually have secured; setting a wage floor above local vendor rates can affect vendor selection and pricing.

citations.title: OpenAI Used Kenyan Workers on Less Than $2 Per Hour: Exclusive

relationships.reason: Documented, audited labor standards are the concrete mechanism applying general labor principles to this context.
The pattern's output is a vendor welfare audit report.
